reason: The saved public evidence does not show an observed structural CSV defect that the existing checker detects (unclosed quote, unexpected quote, text after a closing quote, row width mismatch, empty header, duplicate header, empty input). A worked example built on an assumed defect would misrepresent the source evidence, so no page was built.
method: Keyword scan (quot|comma|column|delimit|header|semicolon|tab|line break|newline|paste|csv) over the blurbs of 100 posts in the two saved Manager forum search artifacts. 35 posts matched; the relevant ones were read in full blurb form. No new discovery was done.

findings.quote: Hi, is there any way to import sales invoices from .csv file?
findings.classification: Feature or workflow request (no batch import of invoices), not a structural defect. The 2022-12-06 reply discusses multi-line records and end-of-record markers; the blurb is truncated, so no observed parse failure.

findings.quote: You have To Duplicate Item Header and Its Values 138 Times!
findings.classification: Layout or mapping burden (one row per line item), not detectable by the checker.

findings.quote: You are correct in noting that "Gross amount" should be "Gross".
findings.classification: Header-name mapping mismatch. The checker does not check header names against a platform mapping.

findings.quote: Manager uses a particular format of CSV for batch operations.
findings.classification: Platform-specific format and headers (copied to a spreadsheet). This is about compatibility, which is explicitly excluded.

findings.quote: However I can put more or less colums in the exportfile.
findings.classification: Column selection or mapping, not a row-width defect.

source_gap: products/research/manager-invoice-import-guide.txt contains only 136 characters of navigation text (no guide body), so it supports no structural rule.
implication: Observed pain concerns platform mapping, header naming and line-item layout. These are the areas the checker explicitly excludes. This suggests discovery is not the only constraint: the offer may also not match the observed pain. Hypothesis only.
